title: NOLAN WELLS: THE PERPETUAL HATRED WE NEVER LEARNED

sense.text: Go to the beginning. Eve bare Cain first, and then Abel, his younger brother. “Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.”

“And in process of time”: it took a while. Cain already knew from the beginning to offer up sacrifices of animals. He got tired of doing it, got fed up with doing it, and in process of time he brought “of the fruit of the ground” instead, being disrespectful to the Lord.

Abel maintained his integrity and righteousness and brought the right thing, “the firstlings of his flock and of the fat.” The Lord had respect unto Abel and his offering, but not unto Cain. “And Cain was very wroth”: Cain was pissed, “and his countenance fell.” The Lord saw Cain’s face.

“Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?” What’s wrong with you, Cain? What’s wrong with your face?

“If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?” If you do what I tell you to do, like your brother, will your offering not be acceptable? Cain already knew what to do; he got tired of doing it.

“And if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door”: if you go against what I say to do, Satan is waiting for you. “And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him”: Satan will rule over you, and you will become a vessel for the devil.

You would think he learned: he got checked for what he knew better. Instead “Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.” Not only did he offer up nonsense, he went and committed a murder after this.

When he offered that fruit, Satan already had him. Now he confirms it by murdering his brother violently.

“Where is Abel thy brother?” The Lord was seeing how much integrity this man had, whether there was any part of Cain left that was righteous.

“I know not: Am I my brother’s keeper?” Am I his babysitter? Being more disrespectful. Am I my brother’s keeper shows up in numerous places today, because Cain is back today. Cain and his babies are alive and well today, and Abel’s are too.

“The voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground”: your brother is up here with me. What have you done?

“And now art thou cursed from the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother’s blood from thy hand.” The Lord took the melanin from him, that beautiful brown skin he had. The same ground his brother’s blood was spilled on, the Lord removed from him, so that he would match the blood he spilled. Now he is red too. That’s what happened.

“Thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the earth”: the Lord made him look like a demon.

“And from thy face shall I be hid”: God will never deal with Cain’s race, his kind, that spirit, ever. God will not hear his prayers. He will not be able to repent. He will not get salvation. That is a perpetual inheritance, to be hid from the eyes of the Lord.

“I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond in the earth.” His kind shall be fugitives, meaning outlaws: they commit crimes and get away with it. And vagabonds, because they will be in lands they should not be in, taking upon them races, nationalities and lands that do not belong to them. A vagabond is found in the most unlikely places. In New York we call vagabonds bums: under a bridge, in the subway, in the elevator, in the stairs, in the park, places they should not be, leaving a mess and filth. That’s what the white man does. He is in areas he should not be in, causing destruction and leaving behind his filth.

“Every one that findeth me shall slay me”: people would look at him and say, what’s wrong with that dude’s face?

“And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.”

There is a game called God of War. The main character, Kratos, is a Spartan, a black one, which is accurate: the glorious Spartans are black. The gods trick him into killing his wife and child, then take their ashes and place them on his skin and make him white. That is a parallel to Cain: the Lord said, I will have you match the same blood you spilled in that ground, I will remove that color from you. Esau puts these things in games and throws little hints out there.

But Kratos was deceived into killing his family. Cain wasn’t deceived at all. Cain was the devil.

“And Cain went out from the presence of the Lord”: the Lord stopped dealing with him. “And dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.” That area is Babylonia.

Cain “builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.” It later became known as Unuk, or Unug, and Nimrod came behind him and built upon the ruins of that city, the tower, gaining all the technological advancement Cain’s line already had from the power of Satan. It is the same place, the same region, as Iraq today: Sumeria, Shinar. The old archaeologists came to this understanding; the new ones call it unfounded, the consensus view of modern scholarship, trying to wash away any biblical validation.

He did not build a whole city for his one family. There were many people around at this time, because Adam and Eve had a bunch of children inside and outside the Garden of Eden. He had descendants, children, and took over. He built a kingdom.
This is Cain’s line. Jabal “was the father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as have cattle”: power over cattle, over resources and produce.

Jubal “was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ.” Cain’s line gained musical influence. The righteous are pretty much gone at this point: Abel was killed. Evil is beginning to grow and dominate the earth.

Power over the resources and power over the music, just like today: the record label owners.

Tubal-cain was “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”: every invention in brass and iron, meaning weapons and buildings. Not regular weapons, but high-level weaponry. He taught people how to make weapons of mass destruction during that time, just as he creates them in this time today. That is how Cain’s line gained dominance over the earth.

Tubal-cain is reverenced and admired by the Masons, the Freemasons, who are modern wizards and sorcerers, like Benjamin Franklin and George Washington. In Philadelphia there is a masonic hall with their portraits, hands held a certain way, because they are all wizards. Masons, black and white, reverence Hiram, who provided the resources for the temple, whom they call the son of the widow, and they reverence Tubal-cain because he was a builder. Their god is a devil. Rumour has it, though it could be internet folklore, that 007 in the James Bond movies goes back to two balls and a cane.

So Cain had power over resources, power over music, and power over weapons. In one word: influence. Power and dominance over the world. That is what Cain had back then, and that is what he has today.
Isaac, Abraham’s son, married Rebekah, and she was barren. “The Lord was intreated of him”: the Lord finally heard Isaac’s prayers and she conceived.

“And the children struggled together within her”: there was a battle, a fight, a conflict in her womb. Back then there were no sonograms. She had no idea what was going on, she was in pain, so “she went to enquire of the Lord.”

“Two nations are in thy womb.” Nations goes back to races. Most of the time, when the same parents have a child, the child is the same race, the same kind, as the parents. The Lord said, this is different. He is a Hebrew, yes, but he is not the same as his brother. They are two distinct people.

“Two manner of people”: one will look a certain way, behave a certain way, think a certain way, act a certain way. Twins usually look alike and act alike. These two would have a different thought process, a different look, everything.

“The one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger”: the one that comes out first will serve the one that comes out after.

“And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment.” The first thing Moses tells us is that this child is red. Moses was not there; the Lord showed it to him. Red, and hairy all over his body, as if he were wearing a carpet. “And they called his name Esau.”

He had a lack of pigmentation, like Cain lost in the beginning. He left the world looking like that and came right back into the world looking the same way. This is the birth, the nativity, of the first Caucasian man, the first European: Esau.

“His hand took hold on Esau’s heel”: the battle that was going on in the womb continued outside the womb. The second one, Jacob, is the one who will be stronger.

Moses does not mention Jacob’s features, because he looked normal. He looked like his parents, like everybody else on the planet at the time: black.

“Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field”, just like Cain was a tiller of the ground. “And Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents”: a homeboy. He chilled in the tent, tended the cattle, stayed home.

“And Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison”: despite Esau’s deformity, Isaac favored him, because Esau would hunt and bring home the best meat. “But Rebekah loved Jacob”, because the Lord told her what he did not tell Isaac: I am going to deal with Jacob.

“Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage”: give me that red. He sought food that matched him, and “therefore was his name called Edom”, meaning red.

Sometimes a baby comes out pink and light and the color comes later. Not him: when he got older the color had not changed. Still red, still hairy, and still murderous.

“Sell me this day thy birthright.” Esau was the eldest, the heir to Abraham’s inheritance. “What profit shall this birthright do to me?” He did not care, because he was evil. He did not care about God’s blessings. He swore and sold it, and once he gave it away, “thus Esau despised his birthright.”

Isaac got old and his eyes were dim; he was going blind. He sent Esau for venison, because Esau always brought him the best, “savoury meat, such as I love.” Back then Esau could cook. Over time he just lost all the ingredients, went in them caves, and now it is bland chicken and potato salad with raisins.

“That my soul may bless thee before I die”: the father would bless the children before he passed on. Esau had already sold his birthright, so he banked on the blessing: I can’t get the birthright, but I can get the blessing.
Rebekah heard what Isaac said to Esau. She would make the savoury meat herself, the food Esau makes, and Jacob would bring it, so that Isaac would bless Jacob and not his brother.

“Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.” Esau had not changed from birth: red and hairy all over like a garment. Sometimes children come out hairy and the hair falls off; children come out pink and darken over time at the fingertips and ears. Not him. He stayed the same way. We are smooth for the most part; even black folks who are hairy are not as hairy as him.

“My father peradventure will feel me”: Isaac was blind, so he would feel to know who was who, like Ray Charles feeling the wrist. If I go in pretending to be my brother, I will be found a deceiver and “bring a curse upon me, and not a blessing.”

“Upon me be thy curse, my son.” If your father curses you, it falls upon me. These were her instructions, because the Lord had already told her while they were in the womb that the elder shall serve the younger. If Esau got the blessing, the younger would serve the elder. She was following God’s instructions from the beginning, which she knew Isaac would not be cool with, because Isaac favored Esau.

“And she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck.” She skinned the goats and put the fur on Jacob’s hands, because Esau had hairy hands. Look at a goat’s hair: it is not woolly. It is straight and long, the hair black women in the world love. So Esau had straight, long hair on his hands and on his head, and a hairy neck, which means a hairy back, legs, chest and arms. He was a hairy man from the womb.

She did not say get a sheep’s wool. That would be different. She said get the goat, because your brother’s hair is goat hair. The mother knows her son: hairy like a werewolf, like Teen Wolf. Bless his heart.

“How is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my son?” Hunting takes time. Isaac was smart: “Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son, whether thou be my very son Esau or not.” Jacob was terrified.

“The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.” So they had different voices. Twins often sound alike, even when they look different. Not Esau and Jacob: two manner of people. “And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau’s hands: so he blessed him.”

“The smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the Lord hath blessed”: you smell like Esau, it is you.

“Therefore God give thee of the dew of heaven”: wherever dew falls is yours, and dew falls everywhere. “And the fatness of the earth”: the milk, the honey, the crops, the best of the earth. “And plenty of corn and wine.”

“Let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee: be lord over thy brethren, and let thy mother’s sons bow down to thee”: Esau’s children will bow down to you and serve you. Esau knew what this blessing was. He said of the birthright, I don’t care about that, but that blessing he wanted. For the elder to serve the younger, as the Lord told Rebekah, the blessing had to go to Jacob. “Cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee.”

As soon as Jacob walked out the door, Esau came walking right in. Look at God. “Who art thou?” “And Isaac trembled very exceedingly”: who did I bless, if it wasn’t you? “Yea, and he shall be blessed.”

Esau “cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry”; he was hysterical. “Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath taken away thy blessing”: your brother came slick. His name means to supplant: he took your place.

“For he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright.” Did Jacob supplant Esau twice? No. Esau lied. He sold the birthright and despised it, and then told his father otherwise for a pity party. The blessing was taken, yes, but under his mother’s orders, because the Most High moved her to do it.

“Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants”: all your children are going to serve his children. I gave him the dew of heaven and the fatness of the earth; what can I possibly give you? “Hast thou but one blessing, my father?” And Esau wept again.

“Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above”: the same thing he blessed Jacob with in verse 28. Watch the difference: “And by thy sword shalt thou live.” How would he acquire it? Murder. That is Satan, not God. It is what the Lord told Cain: I will hide my face from you. This is not from me; it is by your hands.

So what Isaac gave him was the same thing given in the beginning: the power to destroy and make weapons. He repeated the agriculture and passed on the curse God gave Cain in Genesis 4.

“And shalt serve thy brother”: that he cannot change or undo. “And it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.” Our people went into sin, and the only way Esau could go free was if Israel got conquered and overthrown. Once we were conquered, Esau got out from under our dominion, built up his power and became the devil he is today, that we serve now. We have served him since the time of the Greeks and Romans, the Spanish, French, Dutch, Germans, Swedes, and the Israelis.

“And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing.” “Esau said in his heart”: in his mind. “Then will I slay my brother Jacob.” Sound familiar? When dad is dead, I’m going to kill this guy. That is Cain again.

“And these words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah.” By whom? The words were in his heart, in his mind. God was talking to Rebekah; the Lord was dealing with her on a high level. That is why she said, upon me be thy curse. The Lord moved through her to have all this go the way the Most High wanted it to go.

This is all predestination. There was no trickery. Jacob was not a trickster; it was not his plan. His mother was moved by the spirit to do it. The Arabs say Jacob was evil, a trickster, because God did not choose them either. Ishmael is our evil older uncle, just like Esau.

“Flee thou to Laban my brother to Haran; and tarry with him a few days, until thy brother’s fury turn away.” Esau’s anger did turn away, but his children’s did not. The hatred he had for Jacob remained dormant in him, and he passed it on to his children.

“Why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?” If he kills you, God will kill him, and I lose you both.
“Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel.” Amalek is the children of Esau, his descendants: the dukes, the elite of Esau’s children. They fought with us.

Moses sent Joshua to fight and stood on top of the hill with the rod of God and overlooked the battle. “When Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.” When he got tired we started losing. So they put a stone under him, and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, one on each side, “until the going down of the sun”: the whole day. Moses was fighting with them in his way.
“And Joshua discomfited Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.” We won.
“Write this for a memorial in a book”: “for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.”

“The Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation”: God will hate him forever. It is the same thing Malachi said, but this is in the law, and we don’t read Exodus 17. God will war with Esau forever, through us, and eventually himself when he gets back here.

“Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother.” The apologists love to pull this one on us, which means they agree Esau is the white man when they pull it.

Why is the Lord speaking about Esau and the Egyptian in the same breath? The Egyptians were our oppressors. Moses saw the beginning, the middle ages and the end of time. He saw who would be our Egypt in this time, doing what was done to us early in Exodus. Don’t hate them, because eventually you are going to have to serve them and be under their rulership. If it be possible, be at peace with all men. That is what Moses is saying here.
“Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way.” God does not forget. This goes back to Exodus 17 and gives more detail on how Amalek attacked us.

“How he met thee by the way, and smote the hindmost of thee”: he crept on us and attacked from behind. In a caravan the strong and mighty men are in the front; the elderly, the babies and the women are in the back. Being a weak coward, rather than attack us head on, Esau attacked from behind. So he was killing our women, our grandparents, the elderly, the lame, the children. Esau was an evil, cowardly bastard.

“Even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary”: they watched us walking and attacked when we were tired. “And he feared not God”: they knew who we were. We are cousins; they knew our forefather.

When the Lord gives you rest in the land, “thou shalt blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven”: kill them all. “Thou shalt not forget it.” God said, never forget what they did to you.

God doesn’t forget. We do. Black folks forget everything; Christianity makes us forgetful, willfully stupid. Look at the picture of Jean’s murderer: the judge holding her, his brother coming behind her and hugging her, the court officer combing her hair. God said don’t forget. I guarantee you she will get off.

“Amalek was the first of the nations”: the first nation to attack us when we came out of Egypt, the first we had to war with, was the so-called white man.

“But his latter end shall be that he perish for ever.” The Lord will war with him from generation to generation, but his end is that he will be killed off, out of existence, forever.

This is years later. Moses is dead and gone; we are in the land, generations later. “I remember that which Amalek did to Israel, how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt”: how he crept up on you in a sneak attack and killed your young and your old.

“Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not.” Oh, God is love and forgiveness? Is he now? Not for them.

But this is not the same generation that attacked them. White folks say, that wasn’t me, I didn’t have you in slavery. The Lord said kill them all for what their forefathers did in Exodus. You nations are going to pay for the sins of your fathers, as we are paying for ours. Our God said keep my commandments and laws; our fathers said no, and the curses fell upon them and their seed, and here we are twelve generations of ghetto later, generations of oppression and lynchings and murder later. We don’t get a pass, but the white man gets a pass somehow?

“But slay both man and woman”: equal opportunity. “Infant and suckling”: kill their newborns too, because they did the exact same thing to us when they attacked us from behind. “Ox and sheep, camel and ass.” You would call that petty. Yes, it is. God is petty with these other nations.

Saul numbered the people and came to a city of Amalek. “Go, depart, get you down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them: for ye shewed kindness to all the children of Israel.” The Kenites did right by us, but they were in close proximity to the Amalekites, so: get up out of there.

Saul “took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive.” Being presumptuous, he spared the tough one, their king, an Edomite Amalekite king. Saul and the people spared Agag and “the best of the sheep, and of the oxen”, the cattle they were told to destroy, being stupid and covetous.

“Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites. And Agag came unto him delicately”: Hi sir, good evening, shalom. “Surely the bitterness of death is past”: whew, I thought you were going to kill me.

“As thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women. And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal.” Samuel cut off his arms, legs and fingers and turned him into cold cuts before the Lord. Samuel was a beast. Saul played games; Samuel did not have time for that. Samuel followed instructions. Keep Agag in mind.
Mordecai was “the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite”: of the line of Kish, of the tribe of Benjamin. Him and Esther were Benjamites.

Esther was “the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai”: they were cousins, not uncle and niece. Her parents died and Mordecai raised her up as his daughter. So she is Benjamin too. “And Esther obtained favour in the sight of all them that looked upon her.”

Esther was chosen as queen. “Esther had not yet shewed her kindred nor her people; as Mordecai had charged her.” She did not reveal her race, because Esther was racially ambiguous: you could not tell what she was. The Persians were black themselves, and Esther passed for one. Mordecai told her, do not tell anyone you are an Israelite; keep that to yourself.

Two of the king’s chamberlains, the doormen, sought to assassinate the king. “The thing was known to Mordecai, who told it unto Esther the queen”, and they were “both hanged on a tree.” So Mordecai saved the king, indirectly.

precepts.why:
“Now there was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish.” That is Mordecai’s line. Kish was “a Benjamite, a mighty man of power.” This was not a regular line; this was a mighty Benjamin line.

“And he had a son, whose name was Saul.” So Saul and Mordecai come out of the same line. Go back to Esther 2:5: Mordecai, “the son of Kish, a Benjamite.” Keep that in mind against Agag.

sense.text: “Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite.” Sound familiar? He is a descendant of the same Agag that Samuel hewed in pieces. Haman is an Amalekite, an Edomite. The king “set his seat above all the princes”: an Edomite was second over Persia, the right-hand man of the king.

“And all the king’s servants, that were in the king’s gate, bowed, and reverenced Haman”, “But Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence.” That is not our custom; we don’t bow to any man. The servants told him daily, the king’s order is to bow down to Haman, “and he hearkened not unto them”, “for he had told them that he was a Jew.”

“Then was Haman full of wrath”: everyone is bowing, and the only one standing up is Mordecai. “He thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for they had shewed him the people of Mordecai.” Now it is exposed: he learns what race Mordecai comes from. “Wherefore Haman sought to destroy all the Jews that were throughout the whole kingdom”: all of them, for what one Jew would not do.

Why? Remember what King Saul was sent to do: kill all of Amalek. Haman knew. They had the records. This is Saul’s people, the race that tried to kill off my forefather, so I will kill them all. That is the proof: white folks don’t forget. Negroes do.

Esau forgave Jacob, but his children don’t forget. Black people say, I don’t see color. Esau does. It’s called red: it is blood. Negroes don’t see color except when they are driving: red light, green light, yellow light.

We are to learn from the writings of our forefathers. Esau doesn’t forget, but we do, because we are not tapped into the scriptures.

Agag was not supposed to be kept alive in the first place. “And Agag came unto him delicately. And Agag said, Surely the bitterness of death is past.” King Saul trusted the enemy, but Samuel did not: “As thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women.”

precepts.why:
“Never trust thine enemy.” That is what Samuel applied, the example he left for us when it comes to our enemies, and it is what we have got to learn to apply. Brothers like Brandon Tatum don’t understand the wisdom that is in the scriptures.

“For like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness. Though he humble himself, and go crouching”: isn’t that what Agag did? He came delicately, crouching. “Yet take good heed and beware of him, and thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass, and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.”

When we apply what the scriptures show us, we will never forget what our enemies have done to us in the past. Our enemies have always been the same from day one, and they are never going to change.

sense.text:
Aman is Haman, “that excelled in wisdom among us”, and “had the honour of the second place in the kingdom.”

An Edomite, Chucky, came in online asking whether Wakanda is real. Wakanda is as real as you being a real Jew, as real as you being the children of God. Chucky, like the doll with the blue eyes and the red hair, like his forefather. That is you: Haman, trying to kill us.

“There was scattered a certain malicious people, that had laws contrary to all nations, and continually despised the commandments of kings.” That is Haman slandering us, saying we are a malicious people, that we are violent. Same thing today.

“So as the uniting of our kingdoms, honourably intended by us, cannot go forward”: as long as these Jews are around, our kingdoms cannot unite. Haman was a Greek, a Macedonian Edomite, saying the Persians and the Greeks cannot come together as long as these Jews are around.

“This people alone is continually in opposition unto all men”, “working all the mischief they can, that our kingdom may not be firmly established.” As long as these Israelites are around, there cannot be a United States. That is why they come into our rooms to disrupt the class.

“But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” This is God talking to the wicked, who hates instruction and casts his words behind him.

“When thou sawest a thief, then thou consentedst with him”: when Columbus came to America, all the Europeans gave consent. Go ahead and conquer, colonize and destroy. The Berlin Conference: carve Africa up in pieces, you take your piece, I take my piece. They all got together and stole together. “And hast been partaker with adulterers”: rapists, murderers.
“Thou givest thy mouth to evil, and thy tongue frameth deceit”: by law, through the judicial system, through legislation and executive orders.

“Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.” This is Esau and Jacob, Cain and Abel. They slander us and lie on us: black people do the most crime. Most white deaths are at the hands of other white people. Blacks are violent? How many nuclear bombs have we dropped? How many animals have we killed into extinction, how many races? Who forced a vaccine on people by law for three years and then said stop taking it? Who drops bombs on a little girls’ school in Iran and on innocent people in Gaza? Who bombed Black Wall Street and burned down Rosewood? Not us.

The same in the short played in class: a white man says, you want reparations, we pay for your EBT, your DEI, your affordable housing. The answer: white women are the main beneficiaries of DEI, over 60% of SNAP beneficiaries are white, over half of those who commit tax fraud are white, and most tax cuts go to white families. They are the ones who exploit welfare, SNAP and EBT, teaching their children how to exploit it, the whole family in one house with one person working; they won’t get rid of it because they are on it. That is what Esau does: he slanders his mother’s son.

“These things hast thou done, and I kept silence”: God allowed it because we are in sin.

“Thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself.” Because God sat back and allowed this man to conquer the earth by blood, warfare and destruction, he thinks God is him: that God looks like him, Christ looks like him, the angels look like him. Surely God is with me, I did all this killing. No, sir. He doesn’t.

“But I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes”: you are watching it now, us being set in order before your eyes.
“Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver.” When God comes back, he is going to destroy them all.

“In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil.” The devil has kids. That is Cain’s children back then, and Esau’s children today.

“Whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God”: that is Cain and Esau. “Neither he that loveth not his brother”: did Cain hate his brother? Yes. Does Esau hate his brother? Yes.

“That we should love one another. Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one”: he was of Satan. “And slew his brother”: Cain killed his brother because he hated him. “Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.”

precepts.why:
Christ says the same exact thing John says, that Cain “was of that wicked one.” “Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do.” Christ said this to his own people, the leaders, the Pharisees, who were in bed with Rome, in allegiance to Rome, who had the spirit of Esau upon them. Like the Jason Whitlocks and Brandon Tatums, the Al Sharptons and Jesse Jacksons, Pastor Pam: these guys are coons.

“He was a murderer from the beginning.” Who was a murderer from the beginning? Cain. And Christ calls him the devil.

“And abode not in the truth”: in process of time Cain brought forth fruit; he did not abide. Neither did Esau. Isaac taught Esau the laws and commandments, and Esau said the hell with that.

“Because there is no truth in him”: in Cain, and in the spirit of our people who love Esau today, like Brandon Tatum. He is a devil too: a strawberry Oreo, red inside and black outside.

Wisdom “preserved the first formed father of the world”, Adam, “and gave him power to rule all things.”

“But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.” Cain, the unrighteous, went away from wisdom. The same violent way Cain killed Abel was the way he was killed. Live by the sword, die by the sword.

sense.text:
“For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he did pursue his brother with the sword”: Esau pursued us with the sword. “And did cast off all pity”: he did not care.

“And his anger did tear perpetually.” The anger Esau had for Jacob back then passed on. That hatred remained. The hatred they have for us is generational: it is in their blood, in their biology, to hate us. They can’t help themselves. They shot a seven-year-old boy some thirty times. They pinned a brother down, a woman called taser, and a white man put a gun to his face and shot him three times, live on camera. Esau will shoot us five, six, seven times while we are not moving: stop resisting. But when Esau fights with them over the gun, they won’t shoot him at all; one cop even ran from him. Two manner of people.

“And he kept his wrath for ever.” Esau keeps his hatred toward us forever. It has not changed in him or in his children.
“Set thy face against mount Seir.” Seir is Edom. “Behold, O mount Seir, I am against thee”, “and I will make thee most desolate. I will lay thy cities waste.”

“Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred”: what Amos said, his anger did tear perpetually. Esau, the European man, whose biblical name is Edom, has had a perpetual hatred, “and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end.” The time our iniquity had an end, brought to modern time, was the so-called emancipation. Look what continued after it.

1998, Jasper, Texas: James Byrd Jr., 49, walking home, accepted a ride from three white men in a pickup truck. You cannot trust these people. Our people are too trusting. We don’t remember, because we are not in this Bible. They beat him, spray painted his face, urinated on him, chained him by the ankles to the truck and dragged him three miles along the asphalt until his head and right arm were torn off, and kept driving another mile and a half, and dumped his torso in front of a black cemetery. Their hatred did tear perpetually. Who does this? It is not in us to do these things to them. They bragged about it. Two were sentenced to death and executed: all praise the Most High, hopefully it was slow and painful. The driver got life, with parole eligibility in 2038. Parole for what? Hoping somebody finds his ass in 2038 and finishes the job.

Thomas Thistlewood, an Englishman, overseer and then owner of a plantation in Jamaica, kept a diary of thousands of pages: over 3,800 rapes of 138 enslaved women, about thirty times each. He branded them, kept a runaway’s severed head on a pole, covered a runaway in molasses for the flies, starved them, and made them take a dump in each other’s mouths, which he called Darby’s dose.

May 1918, Valdosta, Georgia: the mob lynched Hayes Turner, and when his wife Mary Turner, 21 and eight months pregnant, spoke out and said she would seek justice, they hung her upside down from a tree, set her on fire, cut her stomach open, and stomped her crying baby to death. Not one person was arrested. Fugitive and a vagabond in the earth: this is Cain all over again.

“Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom”: “Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle.” “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”, “that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?”

“Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle”: that is what Edom does. He uses the eagle as his symbol: Spain, America, Britain, Russia, France, the Greeks and the Romans all exalt themselves as the eagle, a violent bird of prey, a bird they almost killed off.

“And though thou set thy nest among the stars”: he landed in space. The eagle has landed: space programs, space force, satellites. “Thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” Once he succeeds in that, God starts bringing him down. America is now officially 250 years old, in its age of decadence, unravelling. Good job, Trump. Good job, Netanyahu. Keep destroying this place.

A thief takes until he has enough. Esau takes everything: the house and the people inside the house, their race and their identity. “How are the things of Esau searched out! how are his hidden things sought up!” Through the Lord’s prophets.

“All the men of thy confederacy have brought thee even to the border: the men that were at peace with thee have deceived thee”: that is happening right now. “They that eat thy bread have laid a wound under thee”: eventually his own kind will turn on him.

“That every one of the mount of Esau may be cut off by slaughter.” Every single Edomite. That is the end of Edom: they have got to go. “For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.”
“Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.” The Bible calls Satan a lion.

precepts.why:
This is Paul: “the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear”: all of us scattered abroad.

“And I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.” The note in our Bibles says the lion is Nero, the emperor, the Roman authorities. Paul called Nero the lion, and the Bible calls the devil a lion: same thing. Rome is Esau. Our own people were in alignment with that authority too. It is the white man; Paul is calling him the devil.

“Deliver my soul from the sword; my darling from the power of the dog.” The dog is the wicked elders of our people.

“Save me from the lion’s mouth.” This is Christ on the cross. Christ was in the lion’s mouth on that cross: the Roman authorities. So the lion’s mouth is the Roman, Edomite, European authorities, and the evil Negroes in bed with that authority too, but primarily Edom.

sense.text:
“Behold a great red dragon.” Why is he called the great red dragon? Because this red dragon is Edom, going back to Genesis 25 with Esau: the first came out red.

“Having seven heads”: a European power. “And ten horns”: the ten common markets that made up the original European Union. “And seven crowns upon his heads”: they all gained power and authority on the earth at certain points in time.

“Michael and his angels fought against the dragon”: Edom, the fourth beast. “And the dragon fought and his angels”: his allies fought against the Lord, as the Lord will war with Amalek from generation to generation. “And prevailed not; neither was their place found any more in heaven”: this dragon lost rulership. The European power structure will be destroyed.

“And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan.” That old serpent is the serpent that deceived the woman. But Christ said in John 8:44, ye are of your father the devil, a murderer from the beginning. So this is the devil, the entity itself, and Cain and his children today. Cain is the physical incarnation of a devil, and Esau is too. We are walking incarnations of our God; they are walking incarnations of theirs, and their god is the devil.

“Which deceiveth the whole world.” Captivity is a loop. The first captivity was under Babylon, whose symbol was the lion. Then Paul calls the Romans the lion, and the lion is called the devil. We were in the hands of the lion in Babylon, and we are in the hands of the lion now. Judgment is a loop.

“He was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him”: eventually he will lose power and authority on the earth, be thrown into captivity, and be destroyed.

“For the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.” The accuser goes back to slandering his mother’s son: you are on EBT, you are violent, you want reparations, you are murderers and criminals.

God did not choose Esau; he chose Jacob. So they believe that if they can make Jacob behave like them, God will make them his people. You can’t beat them, become them: I will make you Esau and make myself Jacob. That is what Esau has done.

And his accusing goes back to what Cain said at the beginning, am I my brother’s keeper: I will give them drugs, give them guns, and blame them for it. They are violent, they kill each other with guns: who made the guns? They are drug addicts: how did the drugs get there? They are poor: how did that happen? Any race that undergoes our conditions will do the same things, or worse.

“All that found them have devoured them”: all that found us when we were in sin devoured us. “And their adversaries”: not just the white man, all the nations, the Asians too, the Arabs too.

“Said, We offend not, because they have sinned against the Lord”: we are not wrong; they went against their God. Yet they put the drugs there, the guns there, and put us in the conditions that cause the crime, and still say we offend not. “The habitation of justice, even the Lord, the hope of their fathers”: our adversaries say, they sinned against their God, the hope of their fathers; that is their problem, not ours.

precepts.why:
“Whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty”: they kill us and then lawyer up. Nolan Wells: we don’t know what happened to him; get my mom, she’s a judge.

“And they that sell them say, Blessed be the Lord; for I am rich”, or blessed be Allah, for the Arabs.

“And their own shepherds pity them not”: our own shepherds, in allegiance to the white man or the Arabs, say we don’t care, we make money off of this. Brandon Tatum, Jason Whitlock, Al Sharpton, Jesse Jackson, Jesse Lee Peterson and the rest of the squad. They are in agreement with death and hell.

sense.text: “A beast rise up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns”: the same dragon as in chapter 12, the same exact one. “And upon his heads the name of blasphemy.”

“Like unto a leopard”: he took on the Greek doctrine of democracy; democracy was born in Greece. This empire would incorporate all of the ancient empires before it to strengthen it, and America became powerful in a small amount of time. It is 250 years old, but very powerful. “His feet were as the feet of a bear”: he borrowed from the Persians. “And his mouth as the mouth of a lion”: going back to Babylon, and going back to the devil.

“And the dragon gave him his power, and his seat, and great authority.” The dragon, the devil, is his god. The devil gave him the power to incorporate Greece, Babylon, Persia and the other ancient civilizations, to rule with all wickedness and authority on the earth, with technological prowess. It is not because he is smarter or has a higher IQ, as they say. It is because his father is a devil, and he lives by the sword, as the blessing in Genesis 27 said: he would obtain the fatness of the earth and the dew of heaven by the sword.

precepts.why:
“Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” As he was in the beginning, so he will be today. Over time he will try to hide his rust, but rust eventually shows up on any sword.

James Byrd made that mistake: he trusted a car full of white folks, and they dragged him to his death for four and a half miles. Rub your hand across a carpet fast and it burns; imagine the street, turning to keep each spot from the ground, trying to hold his head up, his skin torn off piece by piece. And you forgive that? Y’all are crazy.

And the list of our people who died with white friends: Nolan Wells, 2026, an 18-year-old college freshman who disappeared and was found dead after a July 4th boat trip to Horn Island, Mississippi with a group of white high school friends. Tamla Horsford, 2018, a mother of five found dead in a backyard after an overnight birthday sleepover where she was the only black attendee. Quawan Charles, 2020, who left home with a white friend and his friend’s mother and was found dead in a sugarcane field. Alonzo Brooks, 2004, after a party with mostly white acquaintances in Kansas. Peter Spencer, 2021, a Jamaican immigrant invited to a cabin in Pennsylvania by a white former coworker and found dead with multiple gunshot wounds, and they called it suicide. An 18-year-old honor student and swimmer who went to Lake Ray Hubbard with white acquaintances and never came home. We don’t learn. We never learn.

sense.text: “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity.”
“I will prepare thee unto blood, and blood shall pursue thee”: I am going to kill you the way you killed others.
“Thus will I make mount Seir most desolate, and cut off from it him that passeth out and him that returneth.”
“I will make thee perpetual desolations, and thy cities shall not return: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.”

“These two nations and these two countries shall be mine”: Judah and Israel, Judah and Ephraim. In old time that was Judah and Samaria on one side of the world; in the future it became the land of Israel and the Americas. I will be a Jew in Israel and a Christian in America. “And we will possess it”: the people and the land. “Whereas the Lord was there”: where God’s people are.

That goes back to Columbus, the Rothschilds, the Balfour Declaration, and the edicts Dum Diversas and Inter Caetera that sent the Spanish crown to enslave the Native Americans on this side of the world.

Columbus wrote in his journal on October 14th, 1492 that the people he found had no weapons, cut themselves on swords out of ignorance, and that with fifty men they could all be subjugated and made to do whatever was required of them: slavery. He did not discover America; he found it where he knew it would be, because he read the prophecies of Ezra, which put the ten tribes of Israel on this side of the world. He knew exactly who he would find here, and he came to enslave them. Wherever God’s people are found, the dew of heaven and the resources are found.

The Spanish regarded the Indians as subhuman, as they did us, three fifths of a man, and burned them alive in the Inquisition. Their land, their possessions and their women belonged to the conquerors. The first voyagers looked for signs linking the natives to the ten lost tribes, and found a Sabbath and the same religious customs. Columbus brought an interpreter, Luis de Torres, who spoke Hebrew, and sent him on shore first, so the first words addressed to the natives were Hebrew. The Native Americans were Israelites.

“I will even do according to thine anger, and according to thine envy which thou hast used out of thy hatred against them.” Where does the envy come from? God did not choose them. They have hated us from Cain and Abel all the way to now. It is in them biologically; you can’t change this man. What God has made crooked, no man can make straight.

And our problem is the other side of it. When the Arabs were taking over Africa, the Israelite queen Kahina fought against their colonization, but the Muslims won, the historian says, by the peculiar Jewish weakness of compassion for the enemy. Forgive, love, I don’t see color. That is how we always get destroyed, hung, lynched, castrated, raped and murdered.

1899, Newnan, Georgia: the newspaper announced that Sam Hose would be lynched, special trains offered discounted tickets, and 2,000 white men, women and children came to watch them cut off his ears and his fingers one by one and burn him alive, and they sold his bones and organs as souvenirs. Those women and children are your lawyers, mayors, school teachers and presidents today. Lynchings were advertised, attended by whole communities and turned into postcards; the anti-lynching bill failed for over a hundred years, and not one person was ever prosecuted. The fugitive and vagabond never changes.

“From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.” We are the kingdom of heaven: the children of Israel. The violent at that time were the Romans.

precepts.why:
“Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man.” That is Edom. “Which imagine mischiefs in their heart”: to destroy, take over lands and take identities. “Continually are they gathered together for war.”

“They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders’ poison is under their lips”: propaganda, lies, the doctrines. They whitewash history and try to destroy the old books.

“Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.” The Bible calls him the evil man, the violent man, the wicked: that is Edom. It is what Christ said in Matthew: the kingdom of heaven suffered violence at the hands of the violent.
“He sent forth his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city.” The Romans came and killed the elders of our people who hated Christ and had him killed, and burned up their city.

“When ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh. Then let them which are in Judea flee to the mountains”: flee to Africa, further into Africa, for safety. Those in the midst of Jerusalem, evacuate; those in the countries, don’t come back in. “For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.”

“And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: the sword of the violent man, the evil man, the wicked: the Romans. “And shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.” Our land is now walked upon by impostors until their time in that land is up, and we are slowly approaching that time now, all thanks to the alliance of America and Israel.

sense.text: “And the fourth came, and overcame all the beasts that were past, and had power over the world with great fearfulness, and over the whole compass of the earth with much wicked oppression.” He gained dominion over all four corners of the earth. Under the Greeks and Romans it was the old world; when he became Spain and Portugal and France and Britain he gained dominion over the fourth part of the earth, America. “And so long time dwelt he upon the earth with deceit.”
“For the earth hast thou not judged with truth”: with lies and corruption.

“For thou hast afflicted the meek, thou hast hurt the peaceable”: the Native Americans, who meant him no harm. I can bring fifty men here and conquer all of them. “Thou hast loved liars”, going back to Psalm 50, partaker with adulterers. “And hast cast down the walls of such as did thee no harm”: Jerusalem, 70 AD.

“Therefore is thy wrongful dealing come up unto the Highest, and thy pride unto the Mighty. The Highest also hath looked upon the proud times”: your injustices, murders, castrations, rapes, lynchings and massacres, that you call riots rather than massacres. Who was rioting? It was a massacre. That is the domestic terrorism of the black towns destroyed: Tulsa, Rosewood, Elaine, Black Bottom in Detroit, Wilmington, Osage and Tulsa in Oklahoma an hour apart, and the Pentagon built on a former black town called Queen City, and many more.

“And, behold, they are ended, and his abominations are fulfilled.” Your time is up. The times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.

“And therefore appear no more, thou eagle”: that is Edom. “Nor thy horrible wings”: his kind. “Nor thy wicked feathers”: all Europeans. “Nor thy malicious heads”: the leaders. “Nor thy hurtful claws”: the military. “Nor all thy vain body”: the whole race is going to be destroyed.
“That all the earth may be refreshed, and may return”: back to normal, “being delivered from thy violence”, the violent man, “and that she may hope for the judgment and mercy of him that made her.”
